questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: The most important factors in choosing my study destination were the academic opportunities, recommendations from previous students, and the chance to broaden both my academic and personal horizons. The host university offered a wide range of interesting and relevant courses that aligned well with my field of study while also allowing me to explore new perspectives and topics. In addition, studying abroad offered a unique opportunity to immerse myself in a new culture, meet people from diverse backgrounds, and gain fresh perspectives that will contribute to both my academic development and my personal growth.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: It was relatively easy to find the information I needed upon arrival. The university provided all the essential information in advance through email. In addition, there were both online and in-person information sessions that clearly explained practical matters, academic requirements, and student services.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: Upon my arrival, I attended a welcome meeting organized by the university's exchange coordinators for all incoming exchange students. During the meeting, they provided us with useful information about the university and practical aspects of studying there. Even before the official start of the semester, they made it clear that we could contact them at any time if we needed assistance or had any questions, which made me feel well supported from the beginning.

questions.answer: For me it was nice to have a space off campus, as I like to have my own place - and there is so many opportunities to meet people so it wasn't necessary for me to live at campus.

Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: The registration process was straightforward. We registered for our courses online before the semester began. During the first three weeks of the semester, we had the opportunity to attend and try out the courses we had enrolled in. After this trial period, we could make changes to our schedule by dropping any courses we decided not to continue with.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: The coordinators from the university were available.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I got all the courses I wanted, even though I was in waiting line for two courses.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: If you have a trail periode, use it and register for all courses you are drawn to - this way you have a better feeling of which causes suit you and your academic interests.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Take advantage of the course trial period. Attend different classes during the first few weeks and don't be afraid to explore subjects outside your usual academic focus. It is a great opportunity to discover new interests before finalizing your course selection.
Be open to new experiences. Exchange is about much more than academics, so step outside your comfort zone, try new activities, and embrace the local culture. Some of the most valuable experiences come from trying something unfamiliar.
Don't be afraid to start conversations with new people. Introduce yourself to other exchange students as well as local students. Building friendships and expanding your network will make your exchange experience much more enjoyable and rewarding.

questions.answer: Meeting new "colleges" with other academic backgrounds and perspectives.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: It took some time to become familiar with the university's teaching style, routines, and expectations. At the same time, meeting new people and creating meaningful connections required stepping outside my comfort zone, but it ultimately became one of the most rewarding parts of the exchange experience.
